newsitem.title: JAPAN: ALPINE SKIING-IOC WILL NOT PUSH FOR HIGHER DOWNHILL START.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-IOC WILL NOT PUSH FOR HIGHER DOWNHILL START.

text.p: The International Olympic Committee (IOC) will not push organisers of next year's Nagano Winter Games to lengthen the men's downhill course, an Olympic official said on Wednesday.

"Everybody would probably prefer to have a longer downhill but we respect totally the concerns for the local environment and the IOC is never going to force anything upon NAOC (Nagano Olympic Organising Committee) in that area," said Francois Carrard, IOC director general.
Nagano has refused a request by the International Ski Federation (FIS) to raise the start of the men's downhill in Hakuba, 50 kms west of Nagano, to 1,800 metres above sea level.
They have said that a higher start would encroach on an environmentally sensitive national park, where Japanese law prohibits excavation and construction of permanent buildings.
Makato Kobayashi, NAOC director general, has said the start would remain at 1,680 metres.
"We must recognise that it is a very sensitive issue for the people here," Carrard said during a visit to Nagano to check preparations for the Games.
The FIS, which said after test events held last year that the proposed course was too short, had said it could run the race from higher up without the usual start hut or other permanent structures.

Both CBS, the American network that paid a record $375 million for U.S. broadcasting rights to the Nagano Games, and Seiko, the Games' official timer, have said they do not need permanent buildings at the start.

"CBS and Seiko might be saying that permanent buildings are not required but it is our responsibility to produce the international television signal and we think it is necessary to have a permanent building for that purpose," Kobayashi said.
Laying timing cables would also require excavation, Kobayashi said.
Construction work would be necessary to connect the higher skiing area to the course proposed by Games organisers, he said. The two areas are separated by a pond.
Kobayashi said Alpine skiers would not tolerate starting from a temporary structure such as a tent.

But no permanent buildings were needed to time and televise the moguls events at the world freestyle skiing championships last week in Nagano, where a temporary starting tent drew no complaints from athletes. Olympic moguls events will be held at the same site next year.
